condition: post thyroidectomy acute supine airway compromise with smothering
level_rationale: Sudden severe difficulty breathing when lying flat tonight 3 days after thyroid surgery alongside 1 cm peri-incisional neck redness represents an acute postoperative upper-airway emergency requiring immediate hospital evaluation and airway management, whereas 1 cm spreading redness around a 3-day-old thyroidectomy incision with mild stitch pulling when swallowing and no breathing distress indicates a localized postoperative wound concern appropriate for an outpatient clinic or surgical follow-up visit.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Core dialect lexicon swap ('have severe difficulty breathing' vs 'feel like I'm smothering', retained in everyday_paraphrase) + single-fact same-case postoperative neck symptom de-escalation control (-cf, L4 to L2).

design_note: Uses four strictly atomic facts (age 51, thyroid surgery 3 days ago, 1 cm spreading redness around the neck incision today, and abrupt severe supine breathing difficulty tonight) with no diagnosis label in any text and an exact 4-word vs 4-word continuous span swap. Replacing only fact f4 ('suddenly feel like I'm smothering lying flat' to 'feel mild stitch pulling when swallowing') keeps the exact postoperative patient, neck surgical site, and 1 cm peri-incisional redness requiring outpatient clinic wound evaluation (level 2) while removing the acute airway emergency with zero stated negatives and unique control wording under Rules A and D.
